extracted.intended_audience: banks supervised by OCC/FDIC/NCUA; bank AML/CFT compliance officers; bank legal teams; regulators and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed interagency rule establishing regulatory requirements and supervisory standards for banks to establish and maintain effective anti‑money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) programs. Includes section‑by‑section requirements, examination/enforcement approach, and implementation expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish and maintain an effective AML/CFT program
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would require banks to establish and maintain effective anti‑money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) programs reasonably designed to identify, assess, and mitigate risks of illicit finance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An effective program requires both establishing (creating) and maintaining (implementing) the AML/CFT program; maintenance requires implementing the established program in all material respects. The rule aligns Agency program requirements with FinCEN and the purposes of the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct obligations — Establish versus Maintain (implementation standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule distinguishes establishing an AML/CFT program from maintaining it; maintaining means implementing, in all material respects, the established AML/CFT program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction affects supervisory and enforcement actions: failures to establish can be subject to enforcement, while implementation deficiencies warrant enforcement only if they are significant or systemic. The rule raises the threshold for enforcement based solely on implementation deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk‑based internal policies, procedures, and controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks must establish a risk‑based set of internal policies, procedures, and controls reasonably designed to ensure compliance with the BSA and its implementing regulations (31 CFR chapter X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These policies/procedures/controls must be informed by the bank's risk assessment processes and kept current as the bank's risk profile changes. They form the operational backbone of the AML/CFT program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk assessment processes — identify, assess, document ML/TF risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk assessment processes must identify, assess, and document the bank's money laundering and terrorist financing (ML/TF) risks through evaluation of the risks of the bank's business activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk assessments should (1) evaluate risks of business activities, (2) review and, as appropriate, incorporate AML/CFT Priorities, and (3) be updated promptly upon any change the bank knows or has reason to know significantly changes the bank's ML/TF risks. Documentation of the assessment is required to inform policies and examinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate AML/CFT Priorities into risk assessments and supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk assessment processes must review and, as appropriate, incorporate the AML/CFT Priorities issued by the Secretary/FinCEN, and incorporation of the priorities must be included as a measure on which financial institutions are supervised and examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FinCEN issues government‑wide AML/CFT Priorities (updated at least every four years). Banks are expected to consider these priorities when evaluating and updating their programs; agencies will consider incorporation in examinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigate ML/TF risks through risk‑based allocation of attention and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks must mitigate ML/TF risks consistent with their risk assessment processes, including by directing more attention and resources toward higher‑risk customers and activities rather than toward lower‑risk customers and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core of the risk‑based approach: allocate supervisory and compliance resources proportional to identified risk. Agencies expect banks to manage relationships by risk rather than declining entire categories of customers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct ongoing customer due diligence (CDD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks must conduct ongoing customer due diligence as part of their AML/CFT programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CDD includes collecting and updating information about customers, including beneficial ownership where applicable (as reflected in FinCEN's 2016 CDD rule), and ongoing monitoring based on the customer's risk profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent AML/CFT program testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks must conduct independent testing of their AML/CFT programs, either by bank personnel or by an outside party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent testing is an ongoing component of the program to validate effectiveness and implementation; can be internal or external but must be independent and documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designate an AML/CFT Officer located in the United States
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks must designate an individual responsible for establishing and implementing the AML/CFT program and coordinating and monitoring day‑to‑day compliance; that individual must be located in the United States and accessible to, and subject to oversight and supervision by, FinCEN (or its designee) and the appropriate Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule specifies duties of the AML/CFT Officer and emphasizes U.S. domiciliation and accessibility to regulators as statutory expectations under the AML Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing employee training program
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks must establish and maintain an ongoing employee training program as part of their AML/CFT programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training should be kept current as the bank's risk profile and AML/CFT Priorities change; it supports staff ability to identify and respond to ML/TF risks and suspicious activity reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written AML/CFT program — availability and bank approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks must have a written AML/CFT program; written programs must be made available upon request and are subject to bank approval processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule requires written documentation of policies/procedures/controls and states that written AML/CFT programs must be available to regulators on request. Agencies discuss bank approval of written programs as internal governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer Identification Program (CIP) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: CIP obligations are part of AML/CFT program requirements, including procedures to verify customer identity and related data collection (e.g., Taxpayer Identification Numbers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal references existing CIP rules and notes instances (e.g., exemption orders) where collection of TIN from a third party is permitted subject to conditions. CIP interacts with CDD and beneficial ownership obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervision and enforcement framework, including FinCEN consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule sets out supervision and enforcement policies, definitions (e.g., 'AML/CFT enforcement action' and 'significant AML/CFT supervisory action'), and establishes a mechanism for FinCEN to review and provide feedback to Agencies prior to certain AML/CFT‑related enforcement and supervisory actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The change is intended to promote consistency across agencies and to focus enforcement on significant or systemic failures, with FinCEN involvement to align with its statutory BSA administration role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold for enforcement — significant or systemic failures only for implementation deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a bank has properly established an AML/CFT program, only significant or systemic failures to implement that established program in all material respects would warrant an 'AML/CFT enforcement action' or 'significant AML/CFT supervisory action.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This raises the enforcement threshold for implementation issues to avoid actions based on isolated, technical, or immaterial implementation issues; however, failures to establish remain actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep AML/CFT program current as the bank's risk profile changes
rubrics_metrics.description: AML/CFT programs, including policies/procedures/controls, risk‑assessment processes, training, and testing, must be kept current as the bank's risk profile changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A program reasonably designed at one point may become inadequate if risk profile changes; banks must promptly update relevant program components when they know or have reason to know of significant changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk‑focused examination approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies and the Federal Reserve Board use a risk‑focused approach to BSA/AML supervision, allocating more supervisory resources to higher‑risk areas and fewer to lower‑risk areas based on a bank's unique risk profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners evaluate whether a bank has developed and implemented a reasonable and effective process to identify, measure, monitor, and control risks; well‑developed risk assessments assist examiners in understanding the bank's risk profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and transparency of risk assessments and program elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk assessment processes must document ML/TF risks, and program elements (policies, testing, training) should be documented and available for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation supports supervisory review and demonstrates that the bank's program is reasonably designed and updated; the Agencies may request written programs and supporting materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer relationship management by risk rather than categorical de‑banking
rubrics_metrics.description: Banks are encouraged to manage customer relationships and mitigate risks based on individual customer relationships rather than declining to provide banking services to entire categories of customers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agencies and FinCEN have issued guidance to discourage broad de‑banking and to encourage tailored risk management based on facts and circumstances of each relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons performing AML/CFT duties must be in the United States and accessible to oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the AML Act and the proposed rule, the duty to establish, maintain, and enforce an AML/CFT program shall be the responsibility of, and be performed by, persons in the United States who are accessible to, and subject to oversight and supervision by, the Secretary and the appropriate Federal functional regulator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory requirement underpins the rule's U.S. domiciliation requirement for the AML/CFT Officer and other designated responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and confidentiality of supervisory information
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule addresses disclosure of supervisory information and how supervisory information may be handled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies reference existing statutes and guidance (and interactions with SAR confidentiality rules) describing when supervisory information is disclosable and when it is protected; supervisory information handling affects transparency and public comment materials.
